$comment: The only view table. The browser reads it, and every offline tool reads it, so a view cannot
exist in one place and be missing from another.
Coordinate frames, because there are two and they are not the same:
azimuth/elevation  the viewer frame: +Y up, +Z forward (the nose). Azimuth is degrees from
+X in the horizontal plane. The left flank faces +X, so `left` is 0.
kernel             the vcad frame: +Z up, +Y forward. Azimuth is degrees from +X in the XY
plane. Right = forward x up = (+Y) x (+Z) = +X, so `right` is 0.
Two numbers per view, in one file, because they are two facts and not a duplicate: the frames
are a 90-degree rotation apart, and hiding one of them in a second file is how the tables
axes        the two model axes the image spans, horizontal first. `zy` means the image's width
runs along Z and its height along Y. The real dimension behind each axis is a role
of the subject, not a name in this file: a car declares length, a character depth.
anchor      how a silhouette comparison aligns the model on the reference.
edge-ground  the leading edge, and the ground. Side elevations.
center-top   the horizontal centre, and the top edge. Head-on views.
center       the centre on both axes. Plan views.
plate       true when the view owns a calque plane, so it must be an elevation.
required    false for a view that informs but does not decide. It never enters a gate.
